title: Quantum ESPRESSO integration and local execution boundary
status_detail: The human response `closeout authorized` explicitly authorizes administrative closeout and constitutes final human acceptance of the completed bounded non-scientific implementation. The accepted result establishes the canonical ksdft2effmass.calculators.dft.pw generic contracts and ksdft2effmass.integration.quantum_espresso anti-corruption boundary; removes the former integration.quantumespresso and io.quantum_espresso.qexsd paths without compatibility aliases; and provides root-confined dry-run preparation, identity-rechecked no-replace staging, bounded snapshots, separate stdout and stderr capture, one-attempt local process execution, version-bound diagnostic classification, native-output discovery, typed calculator outcomes, and Workflow-correlated dispatch adaptation. Deterministic fake-executable software verification, maintained Python evidence conformance, affected and Harness tests, Ruff, MyPy, Sphinx warnings-as-errors, ownership validation, Harness validation, synchronized projection integrity, and independent read-only review support this accepted software-contract result. Real-QE diagnostic signatures remain unsupported. No Quantum ESPRESSO, Wannier90, MPI, scheduler, remote service, or other scientific executable was invoked by this Task; no scientific validation, uncertainty-quantification claim, dependency change, release, publication, or automatic successor activation is accepted or authorized, and no successor is active.
objective: Implement and verify the initial ksdft2effmass.integration.quantum_espresso anti-corruption boundary and its ksdft2effmass.calculators.dft.pw generic port for exact input staging, root-confined local invocation, deterministic workspace manifests, separate stdout/stderr, version-bound diagnostic classification, typed calculator outcomes, native artifact discovery, and project failure mapping.
authorized_scope: Apply the DataObject/ActionObject model to narrowly owned QE serialization, staging, invocation, snapshot, artifact-discovery, and parsing behavior without a generic integration base class.

Migrate demonstrated backend-neutral plane-wave DFT contracts to the canonical ksdft2effmass.calculators.dft.pw public package and all QE-specific contracts and behavior to ksdft2effmass.integration.quantum_espresso.

Remove the former ksdft2effmass.integration.quantumespresso compatibility namespace and ksdft2effmass.io.quantum_espresso.qexsd legacy path; supported QE source, tests, and documentation use only ksdft2effmass.integration.quantum_espresso.
Implement dry-run validation for root confinement, exact argument vectors, separate stream targets, snapshot scope, disk availability, and protected-execution authorization identities.

Implement executable-, QE-version-, and classifier-version-bound diagnostic classification over exact independent stdout and stderr artifacts, with known nonblocking, known fatal, contradictory, and unresolved outcomes.

Return determinately captured calculator-reported failures as typed operation-specific results while reserving rejected or indeterminate dispatch outcomes for applicable integration, capture, identity, and reconciliation failures.

Expose separate process, calculator, diagnostic, artifact, and native-state facts for Workflow-owned dependency admission and resolution-gated retry without implementing retry dispatch in the integration.

Add software-verification evidence using deterministic test executables for success, successful stderr notices, stdout fatal diagnostics, secondary stderr diagnostics, unknown diagnostics, nonzero exit, signal termination, missing executable, before/after snapshot failure, changing files, symlinks, atomic terminal records, cleanup, and nonmutation boundaries.
Keep all Quantum ESPRESSO, optional scheduler, and third-party types out of project core public signatures and persisted neutral records.
completion_criteria: The ksdft2effmass.calculators.dft.pw and ksdft2effmass.integration.quantum_espresso packages obey the documented inward dependency direction and introduce no generic base class or plugin registry.
The former ksdft2effmass.integration.quantumespresso and ksdft2effmass.io.quantum_espresso.qexsd paths are absent and supported QE imports use only ksdft2effmass.integration.quantum_espresso.
A dry run cannot invoke a scientific executable and reports the exact command, workspace, stream, and snapshot destinations.
Deterministic test executables demonstrate separate stdout/stderr, terminal process records, before/after manifests, process-creation failure, and snapshot-failure behavior.

Diagnostic fixtures demonstrate nonblocking stderr, fatal stdout with a secondary stderr diagnostic, fail-closed unknown or contradictory diagnostics, and exact stream and classifier-version identity retention.

Typed calculator-failure and unresolved-diagnostic results are not continuation-eligible, and no integration-owned code retries, changes settings, constructs execution grants, or performs Workflow CPN transitions.
No Quantum ESPRESSO, Wannier90, MPI, scheduler, remote service, or scientific calculation is used in software verification.
Implementation, maintained tests, documentation, independent review, and final verification pass under explicit non-overlapping ownership.
exclusions: This Task does not run Quantum ESPRESSO, Wannier90, PWTK, MPI workloads, remote jobs, or scientific calculations.
It does not create AiiDA or Airflow packages, add optional dependencies, or adopt their runtime or persistence models.
It does not define scientific settings, choose pseudopotentials, interpret numerical results, or grant execution authority.
It does not add a shared integration base class, universal backend, engine hierarchy, service locator, or plugin framework.
It does not implement automatic retry, Workflow recovery topology, diagnostic-driven setting repair, or execution-grant issuance.
It does not commit ignored simulation artifacts.
